overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: five councilors who dined together after a meeting were credited as having discussed only social matters, and the AG reminded the council of its complaint-response deadline.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that a quorum of the council deliberated outside a noticed meeting during a social dinner after a council meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find no evidence that any improper deliberation took place.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the council did not respond to the complaint until the AG's office contacted it multiple times, contrary to the 14-business-day requirement.
allegations.key_passage: Unless an extension of time has been requested, a public body must, within 14 business days of receipt of an Open Meeting Law complaint, send a copy of the complaint to the Attorney General's Office and notify the Attorney General's Office of any remedial action taken.
